rationale: The literature does not support the hypothesis that hypomorphic missense variants in the acyl-CoA binding domain of ACBD6 cause a distinct, slower-progressing phenotype with later-onset dystonia. In the primary disease-defining cohort of 45 individuals from 28 families (Kaiyrzhanov et al., 2024), 18 of the 20 distinct pathogenic variants were loss-of-function (LOF), with only 1 missense and 1 in-frame insertion identified across the entire international cohort. The phenotype across all patients was uniformly characterized by early-onset disease, moderate-to-severe global developmental delay/intellectual disability (100%), expressive language impairment (98%), and early-onset progressive postural deformities (97%) and dystonia (94%). Screening of 1,924 late-onset isolated dystonia patients (Thomsen et al., 2025) failed to establish ACBD6 missense variants as a confirmed cause of late-onset dystonia. Thus, there is currently no empirical evidence for an attenuated or late-onset dystonia phenotype driven by hypomorphic ACBD6 missense alleles.

evidence.text: In a study of 45 affected individuals from 28 families with bi-allelic ACBD6 variants, 18 of 20 unique variants were predicted loss-of-function, with only 1 missense and 1 in-frame insertion variant identified. Patients presented with early-onset progressive postural deformities (97%), dystonia (94%), and universal neurodevelopmental impairment (100%), without evidence of an attenuated late-onset dystonia phenotype driven by hypomorphic missense variants.

conflicts: The hypothesis assumes a hypomorphic missense class causing late-onset, slower-progression dystonia, but 90% (18/20) of reported alleles are loss-of-function, and the only reported cohort demonstrates early childhood onset across all identified genotypes, including the single missense case.
Large-scale screening of 1,924 late-onset dystonia cases did not validate ACBD6 missense variants as a cause of late-onset isolated dystonia.

new_directions.question_text: Does residual N-myristoyltransferase-regulating activity in ACBD6 missense mutants alter enzymatic function in vitro compared to complete null alleles?
new_directions.rationale: Functional assays measuring N-myristoylation via YnMyr chemical proteomics can establish whether candidate missense variants preserve partial acyl-CoA binding activity or act as complete loss-of-function alleles.

new_directions.question_text: Are biallelic ACBD6 missense variants present in unsolved adult-onset or adolescent-onset dystonia registries after deep re-annotation?
new_directions.rationale: Systematic targeted re-analysis of whole-genome/exome datasets from international dystonia consortia can formally confirm or rule out the existence of hypomorphic adult-onset phenotypes.
